the_five_strands.0_account_level_incidence: 6 of 218 distinct maker addresses are in the charged class -- 2.75%. That is the rate at which an ACCOUNT is charged, and it is the number that matters, because charged-ness is an account attribute and not a per-fill event. Our own class is UNOBSERVED and unobservable from this corpus.
the_five_strands.1_account_partition_is_total: six maker addresses are charged on 100% of their legs and none is mixed; charged-ness is an ACCOUNT attribute
the_five_strands.2_the_RATE_is_an_account_attribute_too: each charged address carries exactly ONE rate tier -- four at ~0.099 and two at 0.495, never both. So the fee is not a market parameter that could be read off the market; it is a property of the counterparty
the_five_strands.3_the_venue_field_is_populated_but_non_d: `fee_rate_bps` is present on every trade event and reads zero for ALL SIX charged accounts. It cannot separate the charged from the uncharged, so it cannot be the rule
the_five_strands.4_the_corpus_is_a_sample_not_a_populatio: the audit's own limit: 901 receipts bound observed volume only. An absence from the charged set is not membership in the zero class
the_five_strands.5_no_validated_fee_model_exists: the formula reproduces 110 of 901 taker legs to 1e-6 (12.21%) where the schedule is FULLY observable, with a maximum residual of 0.51 USDC

negative_declaration.our_class: UNOBSERVED -- and unobservable from this corpus
negative_declaration.and_the_sixth_which_is_decisive: WE HAVE NO MAKER ADDRESS. The programme is research-only and has never rested an order on this book, so our own treatment is not merely unobserved -- it does not yet exist to observe. No amount of further collection closes that; only trading does.
negative_declaration.REVIEW_256_SENTENCE_TRANSCRIBED: `fee_rate_bps` HAS NEVER BEEN OBSERVED ON A CHARGED FILL. The field is populated and constant -- REVIEW 256 measures it at 1,881,868 of 1,881,868 trade events carrying the same value -- and every fill the chain actually charged sits OUTSIDE that set, because the charged fills are identified on chain by the OrderFilled fee word and never by this field. A constant observed only where the answer is always the same is not evidence about the case where it differs. The positive controls are what make that statement safe to make rather than merely plausible: the extractor was shown to separate a large value from a tiny one before it was pointed at the question.
negative_declaration.REVIEW_256_COUNTS_ARE_REVS_MEASUREMENT: the 1,881,868 constancy and the control counts are REVIEW 256's, transcribed here rather than re-derived. DA's own independent sweep found the same constancy over a smaller window: 76,617 of 76,617 trade events across 8 UTC days.
what_would_change_it: the published CLOB fee schedule for these condition ids with an effective date, which no collector captures
or an executing account of our own with observed fills

market_facts.legal_tick_caveat: every market record declares 0.01, uniformly across all coins and both months. The BOOK does not match it exactly: 342 of 4171076 resting levels (0.0082%) sit at 0.001 granularity, in 8 of 24 sampled windows -- and those windows declare 0.01 too. So the tick is the right ROUNDING grid and is NOT a guarantee that no finer price rests on the book.

input_manifest.WHAT_A_SEAL_DOES_NOT_CLAIM: it pins the BYTES the chain read. It does not certify they are correct, complete, or free of collector gaps -- gap statuses are a separate predicate and stay one. A seal answers 'is this the same input?', never 'is this a good input?'

candidate_count.WHY_THIS_FIELD_EXISTS: a scratch-dir builder has voided a freeze in this programme before (rule 12). `identity_of` resolves paths inside a temp worktree, so the recorded paths were /tmp; the digests were always of the same bytes, but no later reader could confirm that without redoing the work by hand. The repo-relative path, the commit ref and a COMPUTED match now sit beside every digest.
candidate_count.M_IS_TWO_FOREVER_CAVEAT: m stays 2, and it is worth saying what those two ARE. C1 is not an independent second estimator of the same quantity: it is a BOUNDED PERTURBATION OF THE BASELINE. The wrapper says so in its own words -- `book.value` is `(best_bid, best_ask, bid_size, ask_size)` -- ONE book event, so C1 cannot read a different event from Identity by construction -- and the bound follows: |C1 - Identity| <= spread/2, measured by REVIEW 256 at 0.005 at p90 over 9.4M book states, with the attainable increment structurally capped at ln 2. So the multiplicity of 2 counts a baseline and a bounded perturbation of it, NOT two independent candidates, and Holm across them is conservative in a way a reader should know about rather than discover. C2 IS EXPLICITLY EXEMPT from this caveat: it is cross-venue (Binance bookTicker), so it is not a perturbation of the PM book and is free to differ from Identity by more than the spread.
candidate_count.M_IS_TWO_FOREVER: m = 2 is fixed at freeze and does not shrink if a candidate dies, is withdrawn, or fails to produce a value. Holm is across C1 and C2 whatever happens to either; a multiplicity that shrinks after the fact is selection on the outcome.
candidate_count.MEASURED_CORRECTION: DA 278 binds both candidates to model_version=s60_probability_v1; the artifact binds it to C2 only and C1 to None, on purpose

null_predicate.statistic: LL_g(estimator) = mean natural-log loss over canonical forecast actions; delta_LL_g(c) = LL_g(Identity) - LL_g(c)
null_predicate.test: exact two-sided paired day sign test, enumerating all 2^G day-sign assignments
null_predicate.ties: an exactly zero daily increment is a REPORTED TIE, excluded from the sign count, never silently given a favourable sign
null_predicate.portfolio_day: BTC+ETH mean giving each coin equal weight; action counts remain reported; no action, fill, market or coin is treated as an independent day

all_of.3_native_coverage_gate: >= 95% of Identity-eligible actions for EACH of BTC and ETH
all_of.4_predicates: all population, timestamp, complement and reconciliation predicates pass

accrual.require: the first 10 evaluable complete BTC+ETH UTC days
accrual.starts: the first complete UTC day STRICTLY AFTER this freeze

success_predicate.day_eligibility_is_candidate_blind: resolved by the frozen day/book gate, official resolutions and settlement-verification coverage only. Challenger availability, score, fills or P&L can NEVER remove a day or replace it with a later one.

abstention_reading_constraint_R924.THE_CONSTRAINT_VERBATIM: §6 scores the policy's Identity fallback wherever a challenger is non-OK, so a challenger that abstains EXACTLY where it would have been wrong still improves the primary statistic; §8's 95% native-coverage gate bounds but does not eliminate this, since selective abstention inside the 5% allowance still flatters.
abstention_reading_constraint_R924.mechanism: a challenger is rewarded for its own silence: it keeps the Identity score on every action it declines, so declining precisely the actions it would have got wrong raises its measured performance above its real performance.

WHY_NOT_LANDED: DA 278: draft only until REV 203 returns six of six. `ready_to_land` requires BOTH an empty gap list and that return, and this file cannot measure the second, so it defaults False and must be passed in.
NO_PROSE_ONLY_PASS: §7 forbids one. Every predicate above is computed from a blob at the ref or driven against it; none is satisfied by a sentence.
